_about: Hand-curated exposure tags for the teratogens register, read by tools/enrich-teratogens-exposure.py. A tag says how a pregnancy meets the substance at a dose that matters. Keys are an entry's name, or the start of it when that matches one entry only. Entries not named here are tagged by rule: Pesticides and biocides when the EU Pesticides Database lists the substance or it has an ISO common name, otherwise Work and industry.

medicine.label: Medicine
medicine.means: taken as a treatment; the effect comes from treatment doses

food.label: Food and drink
food.means: swallowed in food, drinks, drinking water or supplements

recreational.label: Tobacco and recreational drugs
recreational.means: smoked, vaped, inhaled or taken for pleasure

home.label: Home and personal care
home.means: met in cosmetics, household products, toys or appliances

pesticide.label: Pesticides and biocides
pesticide.means: applied to kill pests on crops, animals, homes or materials

work.label: Work and industry
work.means: met mainly where it is made or used at work

medicines: Aspirin (NOTE:  It is especially  important not to use aspirin during the last three months of pregnancy,  unless specifically directed to do so by a physician because it may cause  problems in the unborn child or  complications during delivery.)

Alcohol (ethanol) in beverages.why: Drinking alcohol in pregnancy is the exposure.

Ethyl alcohol in alcoholic beverages.why: Drinking alcohol in pregnancy is the exposure.

Methyl mercury.why: Reaches the diet mainly through fish and seafood.

Methylmercury.why: Reaches the diet mainly through fish and seafood.

methylmercuric chloride.why: Reaches the diet mainly through fish and seafood.

Mercury and mercury compounds.why: Methylmercury reaches the diet through fish and seafood; metallic mercury and its salts are met at work.

home.why: Inorganic mercury salts are found in skin-lightening creams and soaps, and mercury preservatives are used in eye make-up.
home.source: WHO, Mercury in skin lightening products (2019)

Lead [Basis.why: Reaches people through food, water from old lead pipes and dust from old lead paint, and at work.

Cadmium.why: Food is the main source for non-smokers, and it is met at work.

home.why: US FDA testing measured traces of cadmium in cosmetics, mostly pigmented products.
home.source: US FDA, Testing of cosmetics for arsenic, cadmium, chromium, cobalt, lead, mercury and nickel

Arsenic (inorganic oxides).why: Inorganic arsenic reaches people through drinking water and food, rice in particular; it is also met at work.

home.why: US FDA testing measured traces of arsenic in cosmetics, mostly mineral-based make-up.
home.source: US FDA, Testing of cosmetics for arsenic, cadmium, chromium, cobalt, lead, mercury and nickel

Nickel (soluble compounds).why: Reaches people through food and drinking water, for which EFSA sets a tolerable intake; it is also met at work.

2,3,7,8-Tetrachlorodibenzo.why: Accumulates in the food chain; food of animal origin is the main source.

Polychlorinated biphenyls.why: Banned, but they persist and accumulate in the food chain; food of animal origin is the main source.

Perfluorooctane sulfonate.why: A persistent PFAS: food and drinking water are the main sources for the general population; it is also met where it is made or used.

perfluorooctanoic acid.why: A persistent PFAS: food and drinking water are the main sources for the general population; it is also met where it is made or used.

perfluorononan-1-oic acid.why: A persistent PFAS: food and drinking water are the main sources for the general population; it is also met where it is made or used.

ammoniumpentadeca- fluorooctanoate.why: A persistent PFAS: food and drinking water are the main sources for the general population; it is also met where it is made or used.

Acrylamide.why: Forms when starchy food is fried, baked or roasted at high temperature; it is also made as an industrial chemical.

home.why: It remains as a residue of the polyacrylamides used in cosmetics, which the EU caps at 0.1 to 0.5 mg per kg.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 66

Urethane (Ethyl carbamate).why: Forms in fermented food and drink, stone-fruit brandies in particular.

Bisphenol A (BPA).why: Migrates into food from polycarbonate and can coatings, which is why the EU now bans it in food contact materials; it is also met at work.

home.why: A hair dye was reported to California in 2019 as containing it.
home.source: California Safe Cosmetics Program, Chemicals in Cosmetics open data

Dichloroacetic acid.why: Forms as a by-product when drinking water is chlorinated.

home.why: Companies reported it to California in shampoos and in surfactant raw materials.
home.source: California Safe Cosmetics Program, Chemicals in Cosmetics open data

Retinol/retinyl esters.why: High-dose vitamin A comes from supplements or treatment; California lists it only above 10,000 IU a day.

home.why: Retinol and its esters condition the skin in creams and lotions; the EU caps them and requires the label 'Consider your daily intake before use'.
home.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/996, Annex III entry 376
by: EU Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety (SCCS/1639/21)
home.basis: The EU's scientific committee counts harm to the unborn child among vitamin A's critical effects and limits it in cosmetics so that total intake stays within safe limits; no authority rates skin use itself.

Tobacco smoke (primary).why: Smoking in pregnancy is the exposure.

Tobacco smoking in pregnancy.why: Smoking in pregnancy is the exposure.

Environmental tobacco smoke.why: Second-hand smoke reaches a non-smoking mother through the air she breathes.

Nicotine.why: Reaches the unborn child through tobacco and nicotine products; its past use as an insecticide is not the exposure here.

home.why: A perfume was reported to California in 2022 as containing it.
home.source: California Department of Public Health, Safe Cosmetics Program data report 2009-2022 (2023)

Cannabis (marijuana) smoke.why: Smoking cannabis in pregnancy is the exposure.

Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol.why: The active substance of cannabis is taken recreationally or prescribed.

Cocaine.why: Taken as a recreational drug; its medical use as a local anaesthetic is marginal.

toluene.why: A solvent met at work; inhaled deliberately, as in glue sniffing, it harms the unborn child.

home.why: The EU allows it in nail products up to 25 %, and companies reported it in 103 cosmetics to California, most of them nail polishes.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 185

pyrithione zinc.why: Was the anti-dandruff ingredient of many shampoos until the EU banned it in cosmetics.

home.why: It was a preservative and anti-dandruff agent in rinse-off hair products until the EU banned it in 2022.
home.source: SCCS Opinion on Zinc Pyrithione, SCCS/1614/19

2-(4-tert-butylbenzyl)propionaldehyde.why: Lilial was a fragrance in cosmetics and detergents until the EU banned it in cosmetics.

home.why: Lilial was a fragrance ingredient of many cosmetics until the EU banned it in 2022.
home.source: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional, SCCS/1591/17

cis-1-(3-chloroallyl).why: A formaldehyde-releasing preservative, it has been used in cosmetics and household products.

home.why: Quaternium-15 was a preservative listed in the EU cosmetic ingredient inventory before its ban.
home.source: European Commission, CosIng inventory (2016 export)

hexyl salicylate.why: A fragrance ingredient, it is limited by EU cosmetics rules.

home.why: The EU allows it as a fragrance ingredient, from 2 % in fragrances down to traces in toothpaste.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 380

methyl salicylate.why: It is the active ingredient of muscle rubs, and it is in mouthwash and flavourings, where EU cosmetics rules limit it.

home.why: The EU sets limits for it by product type and bars it for children under 6 except in toothpaste.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 324

salicylic acid.why: It treats warts and calluses at high strength, and it is in skin-care and anti-acne products, where EU cosmetics rules limit it.

home.why: The EU allows it in cosmetics up to 3 %, and not in products for children under 3.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 98

Dichlorophene.why: An antimicrobial in cosmetics and household products, it is limited by EU cosmetics rules and also used as a biocide.

home.why: The EU allows it up to 0.5 %, labelled 'Contains Dichlorophen'.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 11

Methanol.why: A solvent and fuel at work, it is also in screen-wash fluid at home; EU cosmetics rules limit it.

home.why: The EU allows it only as a denaturant of ethanol and isopropyl alcohol, up to 5 %.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 52

Ethylene glycol (ingested).why: It is the main ingredient of antifreeze; California lists it only when swallowed.

carbon monoxide.why: Poisoning comes from faulty boilers, stoves and engines in closed spaces, and it is met at work.

4,4'-sulphonyldiphenol; bisphenol S.why: It replaced bisphenol A in thermal-paper receipts and is also met at work.

bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate.why: A PVC softener, it is restricted by the EU in toys and consumer articles and met at work.

home.why: Health Canada detected it in 8 of 252 cosmetic and personal-care products bought in 2007.
home.source: Koniecki et al. (Health Canada), Environ Res 2011

dibutyl phthalate; DBP.why: A PVC softener, it is restricted by the EU in toys and consumer articles and met at work.

BBP; benzyl butyl phthalate.why: A PVC softener, it is restricted by the EU in toys and consumer articles and met at work.

diisobutyl phthalate.why: A PVC softener, it is restricted by the EU in toys and consumer articles and met at work.

boric acid.why: Borates are in household products and slime toys, where EU toy rules cap the boron a toy may release; they are also met at work.

disodium octaborate.why: Borates are in household products and slime toys, where EU toy rules cap the boron a toy may release; they are also met at work.

tetraboron disodium heptaoxide.why: Borates are in household products and slime toys, where EU toy rules cap the boron a toy may release; they are also met at work.

perboric acid (H3BO2.why: Borates are in household products and slime toys, where EU toy rules cap the boron a toy may release; they are also met at work.

perboric acid, sodium salt.why: Borates are in household products and slime toys, where EU toy rules cap the boron a toy may release; they are also met at work.

sodium peroxometaborate.why: Borates are in household products and slime toys, where EU toy rules cap the boron a toy may release; they are also met at work.

Sulfur dioxidee.why: An air pollutant from burning coal and oil, it is also met at work.

home.why: Nail glues were reported to California as containing it.
home.source: California Department of Public Health, Safe Cosmetics Program data report 2009-2022 (2023)

Benzene.why: It is met at work and in air polluted by traffic and tobacco smoke.

home.why: Aerosol dry shampoos were recalled in the US in 2022 because they could contain benzene.
home.source: Unilever recall of dry shampoos, posted by the US FDA (18 October 2022)

1,3-Butadiene.why: It is met at work and in traffic exhaust and tobacco smoke.

benzo[a]pyrene.why: It forms when wood, coal, tobacco or food burn.

home.why: An eye-and-lip product was reported to California in 2016 as containing it.
home.source: California Safe Cosmetics Program, Chemicals in Cosmetics open data

dinitrogen oxide.why: Nitrous oxide is an anaesthetic and pain relief in labour; operating-room and dental staff breathe it at work.

Halothane.why: An anaesthetic gas, it is breathed at work by operating-room staff.

piperazine; [solid].why: It is a medicine against worms, taken in gram doses, and an industrial chemical.

piperazine hydrochloride.why: It is a medicine against worms, taken in gram doses, and an industrial chemical.

1,1-Dichloro-2,2-bis.why: The breakdown product of DDT, it persists in the food chain.

p,p'-DDT.why: An insecticide, it is banned by the Stockholm Convention and persists in the food chain.

o,p'-DDT.why: It is a component of technical DDT, an insecticide.

2,4-Diamino-6-chloro-s-triazine.why: A breakdown product of atrazine-type herbicides, it is found in drinking water.

Des-ethyl atrazine.why: A breakdown product of atrazine-type herbicides, it is found in drinking water.

Des-isopropyl atrazine.why: A breakdown product of atrazine-type herbicides, it is found in drinking water.

1,2,4-triazole.why: It is a breakdown product of the triazole fungicides.

ethylene thiourea.why: It is a breakdown product of the dithiocarbamate fungicides, such as mancozeb.

propylenethiourea.why: It is a breakdown product of propineb, a dithiocarbamate fungicide.

Disodium cyanodithioimidocarbonate.why: It is a biocide used in industrial water and paper making.

Potassium dimethyldithiocarbamate.why: It is a fungicide and biocide.

Sodium dimethyldithiocarbamate.why: It is a fungicide and biocide.

Fluvalinate.why: It is an insecticide and acaricide.

Nitrapyrin.why: It is added to fertiliser to slow the conversion of nitrogen in soil.

Oxythioquinox.why: It is a fungicide and acaricide.

Bromacil lithium salt.why: It is a herbicide; the lithium is only its salt, not the medicine.

Tributyltin methacrylate.why: It is a biocide of antifouling paints.

tributyltin compounds.why: They are biocides of antifouling paints and wood preservatives.

silver zinc zeolite.why: It is a biocide added to materials to keep microbes off.

home.why: The EU allows it as a preservative in deodorant sprays and powder foundations.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex V entry 61

lead hydrogen arsenate.why: Lead arsenate is a former insecticide of orchards.

dodemorph acetate.why: It is a salt of dodemorph, a fungicide.

Hexachlorobenzene.why: A former fungicide, it is banned by the Stockholm Convention and persists in the food chain.

Chlordecone.why: An insecticide once used on banana plantations, it still contaminates soil, water and food in the French Antilles.

carbon disulphide.why: A solvent of the viscose industry, it is met at work.

ethylene oxide.why: It sterilises medical equipment and is used to make chemicals; it is met at work.

home.why: Companies reported it in 65 cosmetics to California, most of them hair-care products.
home.source: California Department of Public Health, Safe Cosmetics Program data report 2009-2022 (2023)

2-methoxypropanol.why: A solvent, it is met at work.

1,3,5-trioxan.why: Used to make plastics, it is met at work.

potassium permanganate.why: An oxidising agent of water treatment and industry, it is met at work.

thiourea.why: An industrial chemical, it is met at work.

quinolin-8-ol.why: A chelating agent and fungicide, it is met at work.

home.why: Its sulphate stabilises hydrogen peroxide in hair products, which the EU allows up to 0.3 %.
home.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 51

Chromium (hexavalent compounds).why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: One company reported it to California in a sea mud, a clay masque and a tinted sunscreen.
home.source: California Safe Cosmetics Program, Chemicals in Cosmetics open data

styrene.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: Companies reported it in 64 cosmetics to California, mostly perfumes, hair-styling products, shampoos and body washes.
home.source: California Department of Public Health, Safe Cosmetics Program data report 2009-2022 (2023)

N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: The EU's scientific committee states it is used as a solvent in cosmetics, and companies reported it in 15 products to California.
home.source: SCCS Opinion on N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone, SCCS/1413/11

home.why: Companies reported it in 8 razor-bump and aftershave products to California.
home.source: California Safe Cosmetics Program, Chemicals in Cosmetics open data

lead di(acetate).why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: It coloured progressive hair dyes until the US FDA repealed its approval, effective January 2022.
home.source: US FDA, Lead in Cosmetics

lead compounds with the exception.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: Traditional eyeliners such as kohl, kajal and surma often contain large amounts of lead, the US FDA warns.
home.source: US FDA, Lead in Cosmetics

Methyl chloride.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: One company reported it to California in hair conditioners and styling products.
home.source: California Safe Cosmetics Program, Chemicals in Cosmetics open data

Di-isodecyl phthalate.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: Two hair-care products were reported to California in 2022 as containing it.
home.source: California Department of Public Health, Safe Cosmetics Program data report 2009-2022 (2023)

chloroform.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: It was used in cosmetics until the US FDA banned it as an ingredient in 1976.
home.source: US FDA, 21 CFR 700.18

2-ethylhexyl-2-ethylhexanoate.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: The US Cosmetic Ingredient Review counted it in 20 cosmetic formulations left on the skin.
home.source: Cosmetic Ingredient Review, Alkyl Ethylhexanoates (2013)

diphenyl(2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl)phosphin.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: It hardens gel nail products under UV light, as the EU's scientific committee describes; the EU has since banned it in cosmetics.
home.source: SCCS Opinion on TPO, SCCS/1528/14

tetrahydrofurfuryl methacrylate.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: It is a monomer of artificial nail products, used at up to 38 % according to the US Cosmetic Ingredient Review.
home.source: Cosmetic Ingredient Review, Methacrylate Ester Monomers (2021)

Methyl isobutyl ketone.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: US FDA data and California reports show it in a few nail products.
home.source: Cosmetic Ingredient Review, MIBK

N-carboxymethyliminobis.why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: The US Cosmetic Ingredient Review reported it in 150 cosmetics, mostly hair dyes, as a chelating agent.
home.source: Cosmetic Ingredient Review, Pentasodium pentetate and pentetic acid (2008)

pentasodium (carboxylatomethyl).why: It is an industrial chemical, met where it is made or used, and it is also reported in cosmetics.

home.why: The US Cosmetic Ingredient Review reported it in almost 400 cosmetics, mainly hair dyes.
home.source: Cosmetic Ingredient Review, Pentasodium pentetate and pentetic acid (2008)

home.why: The US Cosmetic Ingredient Review found it in 5 leave-on cosmetics in 2018 FDA data.
home.source: Cosmetic Ingredient Review, Methylxanthines (2019)

home.why: Regulators found it undeclared in skin-lightening creams and toners sold as cosmetics.
home.source: Philippine FDA, Advisory No. 2020-2081
home.basis: The Philippine FDA warns that tretinoin in such creams may harm the developing fetus.

Ionising radiation (X-rays, gamma rays).why: Met in medical imaging and radiotherapy, and at work in radiology, nuclear medicine and the nuclear industry.

medicine.why: Diagnostic X-rays usually give the unborn child well under 50 mGy; the risk lies with high doses such as radiotherapy.

work.why: EU law keeps the dose to the unborn child of a worker who declares her pregnancy unlikely to exceed 1 mSv.

Retinol/retinyl esters.text: Taking more than 10,000 IU a day of preformed vitamin A from supplements in early pregnancy was linked to about five times more birth defects of cranial-neural-crest origin.
Retinol/retinyl esters.source: Rothman et al., N Engl J Med 1995

Alcohol (ethanol) in beverages.text: No amount of alcohol is known to be safe in pregnancy; the CDC says there is no safe time to drink and all types of alcohol can be harmful.
Alcohol (ethanol) in beverages.source: CDC, About Alcohol Use During Pregnancy (reviewed 14 August 2026)

Ethyl alcohol in alcoholic beverages.text: No amount of alcohol is known to be safe in pregnancy; the CDC says there is no safe time to drink and all types of alcohol can be harmful.
Ethyl alcohol in alcoholic beverages.source: CDC, About Alcohol Use During Pregnancy (reviewed 14 August 2026)

Tobacco smoking in pregnancy.text: Smoking in pregnancy raised the odds of limb reduction defects by about a quarter (odds ratio 1.26); the review reports no pooled figure by cigarettes per day.
Tobacco smoking in pregnancy.source: Hackshaw et al., Hum Reprod Update 2011

Tobacco smoke (primary).text: Smoking in pregnancy raised the odds of limb reduction defects by about a quarter (odds ratio 1.26); the review reports no pooled figure by cigarettes per day.
Tobacco smoke (primary).source: Hackshaw et al., Hum Reprod Update 2011

Lead [Basis.text: EFSA found no clear threshold below which lead is known to cause no harm, with particular concern for brain development in unborn babies, infants and children.
Lead [Basis.source: EFSA news, 20 April 2010 (CONTAM opinion on lead in food)
